analysis.title: ETD Rates Watch: Tech Troubles Trigger A Bond Bid
key_insights: Nasdaq E-mini futures were down 2% as of 0700 GMT on 10/30 after Amazon and Intel earnings raised capex concerns. Intel fell 22% after hours and Amazon fell as much as 7%.
Alphabet and Caterpillar were among the largest decliners on Thursday. The desk says the market is becoming more selective about which names it backs.
Asia sold off: Nikkei -2.12%, Kospi -3.48%. USTs rallied, with TY futures tracking Nasdaq futures tick for tick overnight.
TY traded 331k overnight, double this week's average, with block buying in the belly. The desk notes month-end may have contributed.
The SOFR strip was up as much as 8.5 ticks, with SFRZ6 up two. Markets price 18bp of hikes in December, down from 21bp on Wednesday.
SOFR option buyers bought narrow put spreads such as SFRZ6 95.8125/95.75, which traded at 2.25.
Early flows saw accounts selling into the rally. OATs underperformed, with the OAT future down 42 ticks in the first 30 minutes after 0700 GMT.
French inflation came in ahead of expectations while Q3 GDP was weaker than expected and showed the economy contracted.

OATs are due index-extension buying on Friday (Euro Treasury index extends 0.14 years), but two large undisclosed OAT blocks on Thursday looked like sells, one outright and one possibly against Bunds.

UBS (Reinhard Cluse and team) still expects an ECB hike in December and one more in March. They said the press conference was not dovish despite the growth-focused statement. Lagarde said the Governing Council discussed whether to hike, and sources cited three ECB policymakers pointing to a December hike.
ECB members Moulin, Simkus and Kazaks said they see no second-round effects in wages yet and that inflation is not broad-based yet.
The BoJ held rates as expected. Governor Ueda sounded hawkish, saying every meeting including the next is live.

DP World's CEO warned of further price pressure from the Strait of Hormuz disruption. Trucking moves over 3,000 containers a day versus about 40,000 a day previously at Jebel Ali, and costs 4-5x ocean shipping.

The US 7y auction came in line: bid-to-cover 2.46 versus a six-auction average of 2.49. Indirects took 57.8%, directs 32.8% (recent average 26%), and dealers 9.4%, their lowest allocation since December.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech weakness sent USTs bid, with heavy block buying in the belly, TY volume double the weekly average and December hike pricing down to 18bp from 21bp.
tension_points.bear_case: Early flows sold into the rally, month-end may have inflated volume, and the desk says it remains to be seen how long the bid lasts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reversal in Nasdaq futures. TY tracked Nasdaq tick for tick overnight, so a tech rebound would likely remove the bid.
